hints: Look carefully at this structure for the two different kinds of stereoisomerism, optical isomerism from chiral centres and E/Z isomerism from C=C bonds.
The ring carbon joined to the side chain has four different groups attached, so it is one chiral centre giving two optical isomers.

walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as a stereoisomer**

For the same structural formula, stereoisomers differ only in 3D arrangement. The two types to look for here are optical isomerism from chiral centres and E/Z isomerism from C=C bonds.

**Find the chiral centre**

Look at the ring carbon bonded to the $-CH=CHCOCH_3$ side chain. It is bonded to H, to the side chain, to $C=C H_2$ on one side of the ring, and to $C(CH_3)_2$ on the other side of the ring.

That is four different groups, so it is chiral. One chiral centre gives:
$$2^1 = 2 \text{ optical isomers (a pair of enantiomers)}$$

**Find the E/Z isomerism**

Look at the side chain alkene, $-CH=CH-$. Each C of the double bond has two different groups (H and carbon chain), so E and Z forms are possible. The diagram shows the E (trans) form.

The other C=C is the exocyclic $C=CH_2$. With two identical H atoms on one end it cannot show E/Z isomerism.

So this gives:
$$2 \text{ geometric isomers (E and Z)}$$

**Combine independent features**

Optical isomerism and E/Z isomerism are independent, so multiply them.
$$\text{total stereoisomers} = 2 \text{ (optical)} \times 2 \text{ (E/Z)} = 4$$

options.A: Incorrect. This assumes the drawn structure is the only 3D arrangement. It misses both the enantiomer of the chiral centre and the Z form of the side chain alkene.
options.B: Incorrect. This counts only one type of stereoisomerism. Students often spot the E/Z isomerism of the side chain (E and Z = 2) but forget the chiral centre, or spot the chiral centre (2 enantiomers) but forget E/Z.
options.C: Correct. There is 1 chiral centre giving 2 optical isomers, and 1 E/Z-capable C=C bond giving 2 geometric isomers. Combined, 2 x 2 = 4 stereoisomers including the drawn gamma-ionone.
options.D: Incorrect. This overcounts by assuming 3 stereogenic features, for example by thinking the exocyclic C=CH2 can show E/Z isomerism or by counting an extra chiral centre. Only one C=C and one chiral carbon qualify, so 2^3 = 8 is too high.
